extracted.intended_audience: medical journal editors, health journalists, science communicators, and researchers studying media coverage of medical research
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment of the quality of medical journal press releases and how specific elements in those press releases influence the quality of associated newspaper stories. Focuses on presence/absence of discrete quality measures in press releases and news stories and analytic adjustments for source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic study facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence in the press release or newspaper story of basic factual information about the study (referred to in the paper as 'basic study facts').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed using a structured coding scheme; when analysing the influence of press releases on news stories, adjust for whether these basic facts were present in the journal article's abstract or editor's note. The paper recorded whether these basic facts appeared in press releases and associated news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of the main result
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the main result is quantified in the press release or news story (for example, reporting absolute risks rather than only relative measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as presence/absence in press releases and newspaper stories; inclusion of absolute risks in press releases was associated with much higher likelihood that news stories quantified results (reported relative risk estimates in the study). Analysts should distinguish between absolute and relative quantification. Adjust analyses for whether quantification was present in the journal article's abstract/editor note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether harms (or an explicit statement of no harms) related to the study or intervention are mentioned in the press release or newspaper story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as present/absent. Press releases that mentioned harms were associated with higher proportions of newspaper stories that mentioned harms. Analyses should adjust for whether harms were mentioned in the journal article abstract or editor's note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the press release or newspaper story reports important limitations of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as presence/absence of any limitations. Press releases that mentioned limitations were associated with increased reporting of limitations in newspaper stories. When evaluating influence, adjust for whether limitations were mentioned in the journal article abstract or editor's note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear identification of randomized trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a randomised (randomized) trial is clearly identified as such in the press release or news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was one of the quality measures used in coding; however, the paper notes the adjusted model would not converge for this measure and reports crude proportions instead (e.g., 0% of stories identified a trial when the press release did not identify it, 29% when the press release identified it, and 9% when no press release was issued).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a structured coding scheme for quality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying a predefined, structured coding scheme to assess the presence of specific quality measures (basic facts, quantification, harms, limitations) in press releases and associated news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study used two independent research assistants to apply the coding scheme to journal articles, press releases, and a stratified random sample of news stories. This implies a rubric practice: define discrete quality measures, train coders, and use independent coding with a structured instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment for source material (journal abstract/editor's note)
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating whether press releases influence news coverage, analyses should adjust for whether the same quality measure was present in the journal article's abstract or editor's note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study's main outcome (proportion of newspaper stories with specific quality measures) was adjusted for presence of those measures in the journal article abstract/editor note; this is an important analytic and interpretive control to avoid attributing to press releases what originated in the journal source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall press release quality (composite implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate assessment of press release quality based on the presence of multiple specific measures (basic facts, quantification, harms, limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors conclude that 'high quality press releases issued by medical journals seem to make the quality of associated newspaper stories better, whereas low quality press releases might make them worse.' Thus, a practical rubric is to treat the combined presence of the specific measures as an indicator of press release quality and expect downstream effects on news coverage.
